headline: Learned classical energies report large efficiency gains on structured reasoning puzzles
summary: A Nov 12 preprint introduces Compact Reasoning Associative Memory (CRAM), a learned pairwise-energy model that solves structured constraint puzzles through recurrent energy descent. The authors report three-seed test results on Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Unique, N-Queens and graph coloring; the abstract reports 99.996% Sudoku-Extreme and 100% Maze-Unique accuracy after 42 ms and 132 ms of training on one H200, respectively. The paper reports at least 1,000× faster fitting than the compared looped models on these tasks and at least 282× fewer Sudoku inference FLOPs at matched baseline accuracy. These are author-reported results on structured puzzle families, not evidence of comparable performance on open-ended reasoning.
